title: model.json (proposed format, for the research session to confirm)
description: The production decider (steps D2 and D3): where it is served, which input type won on val, and the exact request it was trained on. No secrets: any key is named by env var only.

mock.description: True only for the app's mock.

model_id.description: Name of the served production model, e.g. 'kev-0.6b-prod-c3'.

base_url.description: e.g. the Modal URL of kev.serve.

env_var.description: Env var holding the key in the app backend, e.g. 'KEV_API_KEY'.

decider_input.description: 'answers': Kev reads the serialised answers to rules.json (C3). 'profile': Kev reads the rendered profile text (C4).

request.description: The decision questions exactly as in the production training JSONL. The app sends {state, questions} with state = serialised answers or the rendered profile.

response_format.description: How to read probabilities from the response (research to confirm against kev.serve), e.g. a JSON path per question.

temperature.description: Per-question temperatures fitted on val, and who applies them.

answerer.description: The answerer used to build the training answers. The app must use the same one at screening time.

via.description: Answers come from TRL's own pipeline (rrf.answers), never a re-implemented prompt.

answer_serialisation.description: Required when decider_input is 'answers'. How P(yes) becomes Kev's state text (research/serialise.py).

threshold.description: For binary: yes when P(yes) >= threshold (plan: 0.5).

bands.description: For banded: label to lower bound of P(yes), e.g. {'likely no': 0, 'unsure': 0.35, 'likely yes': 0.65}.

validation.description: Optional val metrics for display (never test).

criteria.description: Option name to description (or null), exactly as trained. Option names must be the template's band labels.
